source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Send command: ipmitool sdr elist
Check sensor will change status when module is removed or inserted
Check SEL will have corresponding logs.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. Temperature should have a normal change behavior.
2. All setting should be correct and match with spec.(including sdr type)
3. SEL should have a correct log when sensor reach to each threshold.
4. System should have correct behavior, like shutdown or change fan speed, when reach to threshold.
5. All STATUS_CRPS1~2 should get pass result.

historical_reviews.deepseek: NO correctly assigns physical CRPS removal/reinsertion to an operator and limits the agent to evidence capture, but it overlooks that the preserved Criteria judge temperature thresholds rather than module status.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: BLOCKED / CHANGED correctly treats the status-versus-temperature mismatch as a semantic block and adds redundancy/recovery constraints.
historical_reviews.round_02: Entry 798/2291 keeps the physical boundary but repeats the incompatible Criteria; duplicate-code entry 1520/2291 is an independent AC-drop case with stale CRPS content.
historical_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: Its non-counting sequence-963 draft was inspected only as history; this review independently distinguishes module presence, input/feed state, load-share recovery and the unrelated duplicate AC interruption.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-35 prevents replacing physical status transitions with read-only observation, ED-36 does not cure contradictory acceptance semantics, and ED-38 reserves correction and verdict ownership.

original_test_intent: The Procedure appears to validate STATUS_CRPS1 and STATUS_CRPS2 presence/status plus SEL assert/deassert through removal and reinsertion of each module. However, Criteria 1-4 instead require temperature behavior and thermal thresholds, so the authoritative acceptance domain is unresolved.
original_method: Use `ipmitool sdr elist` around an engineer-performed CRPS removal/reinsertion. This physical module service is not equivalent to the duplicate row's AC drop and cannot be judged by copied temperature-threshold Criteria.
manual_activity: After engineer correction, a qualified operator services one identified CRPS module at a time under the vendor-approved live or powered-down procedure. Automation may only capture status, SEL, power, feed, redundancy, load-share, thermal and host evidence.
required_inputs: Engineer decision whether this case is CRPS presence/status, temperature threshold, or two separately scoped tests
CRPS1/2 model, serial, slot, AC feed, FRU presence, STATUS_CRPS sensor/SDR, normal/absent/fault values and SEL assert/deassert event data
Vendor declaration of live-removal support and exact latch/cable/feed/service sequence, or an approved powered-down alternative with documented coverage difference
System load, remaining-module capacity, redundancy mode, feed headroom, power redistribution/load-share tolerance and thermal limits
Supported IPMI/Redfish/vendor status read, independent power/PMBus monitoring, maintenance approval, abort and recovery owner
safety_requirements: Do not remove a CRPS until engineers correct the acceptance domain and the exact module/feed/status identity is established.
Do not substitute AC drop, PDU cycling or removal of both modules for a one-module status test; the duplicate AC-drop case is separate.

If live service is approved, verify the remaining module/feed can carry the measured load with margin, reduce workload as specified, and monitor output rails, redundancy, load share, temperature and host/BMC continuously.
Abort on voltage/rail instability, overload/derating, redundancy loss beyond the planned degraded state, wrong status/SEL, thermal rise, BMC loss or host instability.
Preserve first SEL/PMBus/power evidence, do not clear logs, repeat removal, power-cycle or auto-retry, and restore the same serial/module/feed unless the SOP explicitly defines otherwise.
After reinsertion verify FRU presence, status deassertion, input/output power, load sharing, redundancy, fans, temperatures and host/BMC health.
agent_execution_scope: Before correction, perform no DUT or power-hardware action and preserve the source/duplicate conflicts.

After correction, baseline both immutable CRPS identities and feeds, observe the operator's single-module removal/reinsertion, and time-align status/SEL with power redistribution, rails, PMBus, temperature and host state.
Produce independent CRPS1 and CRPS2 presence assert/deassert plus recovery evidence; keep temperature-threshold testing separate if engineers retain it.
Do not manipulate modules, AC feeds, load-share settings or thresholds, infer event meanings, clear evidence, retry or issue PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Correct the Review-layer acceptance matrix for status versus temperature while preserving Master, and confirm the duplicate AC-drop row remains separate.
Approve module/feed mapping, live-service capability, remaining-capacity/load plan, physical SOP, abort and recovery; supervise the operator.
Issue per-module status/recovery and overall DUT verdicts.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Its physical/manual boundary is correct and the source high-level IPMI read is appropriate supporting evidence. It is incomplete because no operator action can satisfy the contradictory temperature Criteria or establish status/event semantics by itself.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: No physical action until engineer correction; afterwards collect mapped high-level status/SEL plus power/redundancy telemetry around the approved operator service sequence.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: STATUS_CRPS1~2, physical removal/insertion, `ipmitool sdr elist`, copied temperature Criteria, script and 5/10-minute estimates remain unchanged.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Correct the status-specific matrix, then service CRPS1 and CRPS2 separately under approved redundancy/load conditions, correlate presence and SEL events with power redistribution, reinsert and prove full redundant recovery; execute thermal-threshold coverage separately if retained.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Engineer-corrected two-CRPS module/feed/redundancy topology and vendor service model.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record CRPS model/serial/firmware, BMC/SDR/PMBus, board and read-tool versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Vendor CRPS live-service, latch/feed, PMBus/status and load-sharing specification plus Project redundant-power budget.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Separates presence/status service from copied thermal criteria and from AC interruption, without changing the Master row.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Read-only status or temperature change cannot replace actual approved module presence transitions; a powered-down service plan does not prove live redundancy behavior and must say so.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Engineer acceptance decision, module/feed/event map, service capability, load margin and recovery.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Removing one CRPS transfers demand to the remaining power path; an incorrect load calculation can trip the survivor and remove both DUT and management evidence.

project_override_considerations: A project may prohibit live removal and use a powered-down insertion/presence sequence, but must record the reduced redundancy/failover coverage. It cannot use the duplicate AC-drop workflow or temperature evidence as equivalent status proof.
expected_evidence: Preserved Master and duplicate-code conflicts plus dated engineer decision for status versus temperature scope
CRPS1/2 model/serial/slot/AC-feed/status/SDR/SEL map and live-service capability
Approved load/headroom/redundancy calculation, physical SOP, operator authorization, abort and recovery
Per-module baseline/removed/reinserted status, SEL, input/output power, load share, rails, temperature/fan and host/BMC timeline
Separate presence/status result and any separately authorized thermal-threshold evidence
Secured module/feed, deasserted status, restored load share/redundancy/rails/thermal/host/BMC health and engineer verdicts

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Procedure tests CRPS physical presence/status, but Criteria 1-4 judge temperature changes and threshold behavior. Code Wistron-BMC-00089-V003 is also reused at row 1521 for an unrelated AC-drop cycle; neither temperature nor AC-drop evidence can be silently substituted.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The status target is identifiable, but the preserved acceptance domain directly contradicts it. Until engineers decide status versus thermal scope and approve the service model, physical removal cannot yield a valid authoritative result and carries power-loss risk.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Changes its NO/manual-only conclusion to BLOCKED because the physical boundary is correct but the core acceptance semantics are not.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees on BLOCKED and strengthens module/feed identity, remaining-capacity proof and separation from AC-drop behavior.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: Adds live-versus-powered-down coverage differences, immutable serial/feed evidence and explicit redistribution/load-share recovery.

review_improvement: Ensures each CRPS presence event is judged by status, SEL and redundant-power recovery rather than unrelated temperature boilerplate or an AC interruption.
independent_technical_reasoning: A CRPS removal is a discrete presence and power-topology change. Temperature may remain normal or change only as a collateral effect, so it cannot define the status result. Because the action shifts load to the survivor, the decision and recovery contract must be resolved before any operator touches the module.
